Quick engineering summary from our side after initial log review and correlating infra traces (Jira INF-1428 attached):
- Root cause: a cascading queue buildup on the dedicated pool serving Quanta's 'triage' model family. Short-lived spike in incoming concurrency plus an autoscaler policy bug caused several worker hosts to fail health checks, triggering a re-shard and temporary capacity shortfall.
- Impact window: 06:18–07:02 PST.
- Observed: ~17.6% increase in 5xx responses across their observed request set; p95 latency increased to 2.1s. No evidence of data loss.
- Short-term mitigation performed: manual pool expansion + emergency override of autoscaler ramp to restore capacity at 07:05 PST.
- Next steps:
  * Engineering will run a full request-level reconciliation by EOD tomorrow and deliver the verified counts (requests, failures, duration).
  * We will preserve and hand over the requested logs for Quanta audit.
  * A patch for the autoscaler gating logic is in QA; target deploy this week (INF-1432).

I've attached the incident export (incident-20260215-jira-1428.pdf) and will follow up with the reconciled numbers.

— Stephanie
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.ai

Subject: Proposed remediation offer and next steps (Quanta Health)

Lena / Aaron — thanks again for raising this and for patience while we validated the impact. Below is our proposed remediation path based on verified engineering numbers and contract language.

Summary of verified impact:
- Verified impact window: 06:18–07:02 PST on 2026-02-15.
- Verified 5xx rate (sample reconciliation): ~17.4% on production inference traffic for that window.

Proposed commercial remediation:
- One-time credit: $28,500 against the Feb invoice (represents ~18% of the per-hour committed spend for the affected window; see attached sla_credit_calc_quanta.xlsx for line-by-line).
- Commitment: priority bugfix rollout (INF-1432) this week and a follow-up health-check audit after 72 hours of normal traffic.
- Contract amendment: add an explicit escalation path for pool autoscaler incidents and an optional Dedicated Availability SLA in the next renewal for production-critical routes.

Asks from Quanta: please confirm whether acceptance of this offer closes the request for additional remediation credits, or whether you need us to present a range and escalate to executive approval.

Internal notes / approvals required:
- Finance (Marissa): Can you confirm whether the $28.5k credit fits under existing approval and that we can proceed with a customer-facing credit memo?
- Sales/CS (Grace): I recommend we couple the credit offering with a two-week elevated-support window and a joint postmortem call with their SREs.
- Eng (Stephanie/Dev): confirm the patch ETA and any operational runbooks we should share.

If you approve internally, I'll send a formal remediation letter and a DocuSign contract amendment for signature.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
